parts.name: shell body

physics.Basic_description: Large white spherical shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main protective structure of the helmet.
physics.Functional_description: Provides structural integrity and protection for the astronaut's head against impact and vacuum.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the large curved surface firmly with parallel jaws, ensuring contact points are stable on the sphere.
physics.reason: The shell is a thin-walled enclosure surrounding an air cavity for the head; treating it as solid would vastly overestimate mass.

parts.description: Large white spherical shell with a smooth, matte finish, forming the main protective structure of the helmet.
parts.function: Provides structural integrity and protection for the astronaut's head against impact and vacuum.

parts.name: interior lip

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey textured strip visible inside the helmet opening, appearing soft and porous.
physics.Functional_description: Provides cushioning and a seal between the helmet rim and the suit or neck ring.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a primary grasp target; too soft and recessed for stable manipulation.
physics.reason: Foam padding is a bulk material filling its volume, though low density.

parts.description: Dark grey textured strip visible inside the helmet opening, appearing soft and porous.

parts.name: visor frame

physics.Basic_description: Pinkish-white structural frame surrounding the visor opening.
physics.Functional_description: Holds the visor bubble and provides mounting points for the pivot mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the rim of the frame to manipulate the visor assembly.
physics.reason: Frame structures are typically ribbed or thin-walled to save weight while maintaining stiffness.

parts.description: Pinkish-white structural frame surrounding the visor opening.
parts.function: Holds the visor bubble and provides mounting points for the pivot mechanism.

parts.name: visor bubble

physics.Basic_description: Lime-green/yellow transparent curved shield covering the face area.
physics.Functional_description: Protects eyes from solar radiation and micrometeoroids while allowing visibility.
physics.Grasped_description: Avoid grasping directly to prevent scratching the optical surface; grasp frame instead.
physics.reason: Visors are thin shells of polycarbonate; a solid block of this size would be impossibly heavy.

parts.description: Lime-green/yellow transparent curved shield covering the face area.
parts.function: Protects eyes from solar radiation and micrometeoroids while allowing visibility.

physics.Functional_description: Allows the astronaut to rotate and lock the visor in position.
physics.Grasped_description: Pinch the knob to rotate the visor.
physics.reason: Small mechanical fasteners/knobs are typically solid metal or dense plastic.

parts.name: inner visor frame

physics.Basic_description: Brown internal frame structure visible inside the helmet.
physics.Functional_description: Supports the inner sun visor mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component, not accessible for external grasping.
physics.reason: Internal support frames are lightweight thin-walled structures.

parts.description: Brown internal frame structure visible inside the helmet.
parts.function: Supports the inner sun visor mechanism.

parts.name: inner visor lens

physics.Basic_description: Maroon/dark tinted curved lens inside the main visor.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as a sun visor to reduce glare inside the helmet.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal optical component, do not grasp.
physics.reason: Like the outer visor, this is a thin shell.

parts.description: Maroon/dark tinted curved lens inside the main visor.
parts.function: Acts as a sun visor to reduce glare inside the helmet.

parts.name: locking ring body

physics.Basic_description: Navy blue ring component at the very bottom, part of the neck interface.
physics.Functional_description: Engages with the suit neck ring to create a pressure-tight seal.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the outer circumference to lift or rotate the helmet relative to the suit.
physics.reason: Structural ring component, hollow to allow neck passage and save weight.

parts.description: Navy blue ring component at the very bottom, part of the neck interface.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
